cluster_name: ESO v2 graph queries on the REAL x79 codegraph
goal: Measure whether ESO v2 graph queries (Q1 read-set, Q4 endpoint permissions, Q5 slice tenant boundary) answer correctly on the real x79 graph, using an honest importer from codegraph.db into the ESO graph schema.
verdict_rationale: The importer is buildable and faithful (101,525/101,525 nodes, 188,090/188,090 edges, 0 fabricated rows), so this is not BLOCKED. The queries are the problem. Q1 (the flagship read-set query) never answers on the real graph: with a graph-derived completeness it returns REFUSED/NO_COVERAGE in 3/3 honest configurations (extractor's own value 0.0; strict BR-05 measurement 0.0049; charitable measurement 0.0135 — floor is 0.80), and the ONLY runs that produce a read set are those where the caller supplies completeness 0.85-1.00 by hand. When forced to answer, Q1 reaches recall 1.0 (10/10 grep-verified call sites) only after collapsing six of the real graph's eight edge kinds (calls/imports/instantiates/extends/implements/decorates -> references); under a faithful mapping it returns 3 files containing 0 of the 10 call sites. Precision is 0.20 capped / 0.10 uncapped because traversal is undirected depth-2 with no relation filter, and the 50-file cap silently discards 49 of 99 real neighbours. Independently, Q1 is a silent no-op on the storage named in the product's own stack: q1-readset.mjs calls db.all(sql, params), bun:sqlite's Database has no .all(), the typeof guard falls through and Q1 returns {status:'ready', readSet:[]} — a false 'nothing to read' on a symbol with 19 real call sites. Q4 produces no real answer at all: endpoint->permission->grant does not exist in the real graph (0 grant nodes, 0 permission nodes of persistence kind), so 19/47 real endpoints throw NO_GRANT_PATH, 28/47 return PERM_UNDECLARED, 0/47 are answered, and the one 'answered' result required a caller-invented grant row. Q5 is the only query with a correct real answer (whole-slice: touches_tenant=true with 6 real evidence rows, and the 0.70 boundary behaves as specified), but it is a veto function on caller-supplied booleans: it has no per-table unknown, so it answers touches_tenant=false at coverage 1.0 for the real category_attributes junction collection, which is tenant-scoped through its parents.

key_questions_answered.can_an_honest_importer_be_built: Yes. Real nodes/edges map 1:1 into graph_node/graph_edge with zero dropped rows and zero invented rows. The only loss is ESO's relation vocabulary (3 relations) which cannot name 6 of the real graph's 8 edge kinds.
key_questions_answered.does_q1_answer_correctly_on_the_real_gra: No. It refuses in every honest configuration, and when forced its read set has precision 0.20 and includes the correct call sites only under a charitable relation collapse.
key_questions_answered.does_q4_return_a_real_answer_unknown_or_: It throws (NO_GRANT_PATH) for the 19 real endpoints that declare a permission, returns unknown/PERM_UNDECLARED for the other 28, and answers 0. The system's true answer (tier decorator + guard) is in the graph but not expressible in Q4's model.
key_questions_answered.does_q5_return_a_real_answer_unknown_or_: Real answer on the whole slice (touches_tenant=true, 6 evidence rows), unknown/EMPTY_SLICE if fed only graph-native 'table' nodes (the graph has 0), and a wrong answer (false) on the real junction-table slice.

subject.copy_used: /tmp/eso-dd/codegraph.db (db + wal + shm copied; repo untouched; no network)

steps: 1. Copied codegraph.db (+wal/shm) to /tmp/eso-dd; all work read-only against the repo and x79.

2. Inspected the real schema (nodes/edges/files/unresolved_refs) before writing anything - the ESO schema (graph_node/graph_edge/source_claim/completeness) shares no table names with it, so an importer is mandatory.

3. Wrote /tmp/eso-dd/import.mjs (bun:sqlite): creates the ESO schema from the repo's SCHEMA_SQL and maps every real node/edge row; keeps the real edge id as 'cg:<id>' so provenance is traceable; stores real kind + line + provenance in metadata_json; records (does not fabricate) the 10 files that have no kind=file node.
4. Built two relation-mapping variants so the result is not an artefact of one mapping (strict = faithful, broad = charitable).
5. Picked one real target with real callers: the exported decorator `Restrict` (backend/mu-infra-lib/src/security/decorators/restrict.decorator.ts).

6. Established ground truth by grep/read in x79: 19 `@Restrict(` application sites across 10 controller files (matches the graph's 19 calls and 19 decorates edges exactly), plus the metadata-key consumer restriction.guard.ts and the dependency restriction-tier.enum.ts.
7. Ran queryReadSet under 7 storage/completeness configurations x 2 mapping variants, scoring precision/recall against GT.
8. Ran queryEndpointPermissions and querySliceTenantBoundary on one real slice (backend/mu-catalog/src/@modules/master-data) with inputs derived from real rows.

importer_mapping.graph_edge_strict: contains->declares, references->references, calls/imports/instantiates/extends/implements/decorates kept verbatim (invisible to Q1 because ALLOWED_RELATIONS has no such name)
importer_mapping.graph_edge_broad: contains->declares; calls/instantiates/extends/implements/decorates/imports/references -> references (a call/import/decorate IS a reference to the symbol; ESO has no finer relation)
importer_mapping.not_mapped: source_claim left empty (real graph has no claim/evidence concept); no row invented in any table

completeness_derivations.extractor_note: extractProjectGraph calls calculateCompleteness('Q1',{file:{covered,total}}); K(Q1)=[file,class,method]; the missing class/method keys default to ratio 0, so value is min(1,0,0)=0 for ANY manifest - measured 0 with 7339/7339 files parsed
completeness_derivations.strict_br05_measure_0.0049: every node in a file that has >=1 failed unresolved_ref is uncovered: file 711/7329, class 72/6195, method 83/16861 -> min 0.00492
completeness_derivations.charitable_measure_0.0135: only unresolved refs whose name actually exists as a node (47,314 of 190,021 = true resolution misses, not external packages): file 1014/7329, class 158/6195, method 227/16861 -> min 0.01346
completeness_derivations.reference_resolution_rate: 94,462 resolved reference-kind edges / (94,462 + 190,021 unresolved) = 0.332; charitable (in-graph names only) = 94,462/(94,462+47,314) = 0.666

ground_truth.how_established: grep -rlnF '@Restrict(' over backend/ frontend/ excluding node_modules/dist/build, then per-line read to drop the jsdoc mention in restriction.guard.ts; cross-checked against nodes/edges in codegraph.db
ground_truth.graph_agrees_with_gt: yes: 19 calls edges and 19 decorates edges into the Restrict node, sourced from exactly the 10 files above, plus 10 imports edges - the real graph's direct caller data is correct, so any Q1 failure below is not a data defect

precision_recall_table.note: silent no-op: db.all is not a function, typeof guard returns empty read set

precision_recall_table.config: adapter, completeness row persisted then read from table
precision_recall_table.note: works ONLY with the adapter; under raw bun:sqlite the completeness-table lookup is swallowed by an empty catch
20 nodes share the name findAll; the real caller file is not in the returned 50

q1_readset.reported_completeness_vs_measured: Q1 reports coverage 0.85/0.90/1.00 in the only runs that return a read set - every one of those values was supplied by the caller; the values derivable from the real graph are 0.0 (extractor), 0.0049 (strict BR-05), 0.0135 (charitable), all of which make Q1 refuse. The reported 'ready' therefore asserts coverage that was never measured.
q1_readset.what_the_read_set_actually_contains: At completeness=1.0/broad it contains the 10 real call sites (correct) plus 40 files 2 hops away that have nothing to do with the decorator - e.g. attribute/cqrs/commands/create-attribute.command.ts, attribute/dtos/create-attribute.dto.ts, all CQRS commands/queries/DTOs of the same controllers. The output carries no relation type, no direction and no line, so a caller cannot tell 'file that calls Restrict' from 'file the controller happens to import'.
q1_readset.cap_behaviour: totalFound 99 -> 50 returned (capped true); the discarded 49 are an unranked slice(0,50) of a Set built in SQL row order (the edge query has no ORDER BY). In the capped run GT-B recall dropped to 11/12 (restriction.guard.ts fell outside the 50); in the uncapped run it is 12/12 - i.e. recall depends on truncation luck, not on relevance.
q1_readset.vocabulary_loss: strict: 72,718 of 188,090 real edges (38.7%) have no ESO relation name and are unreachable to Q1 (calls 30,353 / imports 37,865 / instantiates 3,511 / decorates 827 / extends 107 / implements 55). broad: 100% reachable, but 8 real relations collapse into 2, so relation identity - the thing that separates 'calls' from 'imports' - is destroyed in the store, not at query time.

q4_permissions.worked_example: GET /attributes (attribute.controller.ts:48, decorators @Public + @Restrict(RestrictionTier.GUEST_FULL_PREVIEW)) -> queryEndpointPermissions throws Error(NO_GRANT_PATH: Permission 'Restrict' declared without grant location). The true answer is in the graph (tier GUEST_FULL_PREVIEW, enforced by class RestrictionGuard), but Q4 has no slot for 'guarded by' and no grant store exists in a static code graph.
q4_permissions.only_answered_path: passing grants=[{id:<RestrictionGuard node id>, permission_name:'Restrict'}] by hand yields status:'answered' with path [route, Restrict, class RestrictionGuard] - the grant row is human knowledge; the graph has no edge from the permission to the guard (verified count 0).
q4_permissions.public_handling: @Public() cannot be expressed: mapping it to a permission makes Q4 throw NO_GRANT_PATH too, and the 'answered' branch has no public flag.
q4_permissions.ground_truth: authorization in x79 is decorator+guard based (RESTRICTION_TIER_KEY metadata read by RestrictionGuard, 19 sites); there is no grant table/record anywhere in the codegraph, and none in the runtime model either.

q5_tenant.tables_derived: 8 mongoose model classes found under */repositories/schemas/ (the graph's real persistence units); tenant_marker = has property tenantId

whole_slice_coverage_1.0.gt: grep confirms tenantId in exactly those 6 schema files

graph_native_tables_only.note: the graph has 0 nodes of kind table/column/tenant_marker, so the only input a graph-native caller can pass is []

junction_slice_only.note: CategoryAttributeModel is the real collection category_attributes, registered as a mongoose model, no tenantId, references categoryId/attributeId which are tenant-scoped - 'does not touch tenant' is wrong at coverage 1.0

q5_tenant.structural_note: Q5 does no inspection of its own: it filters caller-supplied booleans (has_tenant_marker || cross_tenant) and applies a coverage floor. There is no per-table 'unknown' state, so a table whose marker could not be established is indistinguishable from a table proven not to have one - BR-05's unknown!=absent is enforced only at slice level.

defects.title: Q1 is a silent no-op on bun:sqlite: it requires db.all(sql, params), which bun:sqlite's Database does not have
defects.proof: typeof new Database(path).all === 'undefined' (bun 1.3.14); q1-readset.mjs line 141 takes the '!db.all' early-return and line 168/158 calls would throw otherwise. Measured: queryReadSet(rawBunDb,{project:'x79',symbolOrFile:'Restrict',completeness:1.0}) -> {status:'ready', readSet:[], totalFound:0} while the same graph through a better-sqlite3-style facade returns 50 files including 10/10 real call sites. The completeness-table lookup (line 99) is also swallowed by an empty catch, so a persisted completeness row is silently ignored.
defects.impact: A caller that wires the product's own bun:sqlite storage gets a confident 'nothing to read' for a symbol with 19 call sites, indistinguishable from the AC-ARCH-02-04 isolated-symbol case.

defects.title: Producer/consumer completeness contract is unsatisfiable: the extractor's own Q1 completeness is always 0, so Q1 always refuses
defects.proof: extractProjectGraph calls calculateCompleteness('Q1',{file:{covered,total}}) while K(Q1)=[file,class,method]; missing kinds default to ratio 0 so value=min(1,0,0)=0. Measured with 7,339/7,339 parsed files: completeness.value=0, perKind.class.coverage=0, perKind.method.coverage=0. Feeding that into queryReadSet -> REFUSED 'Completeness 0 is below floor 0.8'.
defects.impact: The in-product pipeline (extract -> store completeness -> Q1) can never answer for any repository, real or synthetic; the only working path is a caller inventing coverage >= 0.80.

defects.title: ESO's 3-relation vocabulary cannot name 38.7% of the real graph's edges, and none of the ones that matter for a read set
defects.proof: 72,718/188,090 edges are calls/imports/instantiates/extends/implements/decorates - names ALLOWED_RELATIONS does not contain. Under the faithful mapping Q1's read set for the Restrict decorator is 3 files with 0/10 real call sites (recall 0). Recall reaches 10/10 only after collapsing 6 relations into 'references' in the store, i.e. by discarding the distinction the query would need to rank or filter.
defects.impact: Q1 can only be right when the importer lies about relation identity; a faithful importer produces a 'ready' answer with an empty-of-callers read set.

defects.title: Undirected depth-2 BFS + unranked 50-file cap: recall is bought with 80-90% noise, and truncation is arbitrary
defects.proof: At completeness 1.0/broad: 50 returned of 99 found (capped true), precision 0.20 on GT call sites / 0.101 uncapped. Noise is real and unrelated (create-attribute.command.ts, create-attribute.dto.ts, every CQRS command/query of the 10 controllers). In the capped run restriction.guard.ts (a real must-read) fell outside the 50, dropping GT recall to 11/12; uncapped it is 12/12. q1-readset.mjs line 233 picks the neighbour of an edge regardless of direction, so callers and callees are reported as one undifferentiated set, and the result objects contain no relation, direction or line.
defects.impact: A precise question ('which files must I read before changing this decorator') gets a 99-file list with no way to tell evidence from context; capping hides exactly the long-tail must-reads.

defects.title: Name-only start-node resolution: Q1 cannot address a symbol in a 101k-node graph
defects.proof: The start query matches id/name/path only and graph_node has no qualified_name column (the real qualified_name is lost at import). 20 nodes are named findAll, 3,767 named constructor, 573 named execute. Measured: symbolOrFile='findAll' -> 20 start nodes -> totalFound 2,374 files, capped to 50, and the real caller file (brand.service.ts) is not among them (recall 0); 'constructor' -> totalFound 1,823.
defects.impact: For any common method name the answer is dominated by same-named symbols from unrelated modules; there is no supported way to disambiguate by file or class.

defects.title: Q4's endpoint -> permission -> grant model does not exist in a static code graph; it throws on real endpoints and can never answer
defects.proof: Real slice mu-catalog/master-data: 47 routes, 19 decorated with @Restrict, 28 with no in-repo permission decorator, 0 grant nodes and 0 permission->grant edges in the whole 101k-node graph. queryEndpointPermissions throws NO_GRANT_PATH for the 19 (e.g. GET /attributes), returns PERM_UNDECLARED for the 28, answers 0/47. status:'answered' was reachable only by hand-supplying a grant row naming the guard class. The function throws instead of returning {status:'unknown', code:'NO_GRANT_STORE'}.
defects.impact: On a real NestJS codebase the query either crashes the caller or returns unknown for every endpoint, while the true permission answer (tier decorator + guard) sits in the graph unrepresentable; @Public() has no representation at all.

defects.title: Q5 has no per-table unknown state, so 'marker not established' is reported as 'does not touch tenant'
defects.proof: touches_tenant = tables.some(t => t.has_tenant_marker || t.cross_tenant) with no tri-state. Measured: slice {CategoryAttributeModel} at coverage 1.0 -> answered touches_tenant:false, evidence []. Ground truth: category_attributes is a real registered collection (mongoose model provider) with no tenantId that references categoryId/attributeId, both tenant-scoped - it is a cross-tenant junction. isImplicit exists but is slice-wide only.
defects.impact: The one query whose job is to prevent a false 'we don't touch tenant' can emit it at full coverage; and because the graph has 0 table nodes, the graph-native input is always EMPTY_SLICE.

discrepancies: The real graph's caller data is exact (19 call sites / 10 files / 10 import edges all match grep), so every Q1 and Q4 failure above is a query-layer or vocabulary failure, not an extraction failure.

q4-permissions.mjs throws on a normal real-world state (permission declared, no grant store) while q1/q5 return {status:'unknown'} - the three queries do not share one error contract, so a turn-path caller must handle both shapes.
AC-ARCH-02-04 ('empty read set, no error') and the bun:sqlite no-op produce byte-identical output, so no AC distinguishes 'symbol is isolated' from 'storage adapter is wrong'.

ESO schema has no qualified_name and no relation/direction in results, though the source graph supplies both - the information needed for D4/D5's fixes is discarded at import, not absent from the data.
Q5's ACs all pass while its real usefulness is limited to vetoing: it inspects nothing itself and cannot express 'unknown' per table.

repro.adapters_note: The 'adapter' in the results is a 6-line better-sqlite3-compatible facade (all/get over db.query(...).all(...params)); it is what the raw-bun numbers are compared against. It adds no logic to the queries.

notes: Scope honoured: /Users/thangs2net/Workspaces/harness-eso and /Users/thangs2net/Workspaces/x79 were read-only; all writes went to /tmp/eso-dd; no network was used.

Two mapping variants were measured on purpose: strict (faithful, relation names preserved) and broad (charitable, 6 relations collapsed into references). The verdict does not depend on the choice - Q1 fails either way, for different reasons (recall vs precision).

Completeness was derived three ways; the charitable one (47,314 true resolution misses instead of 190,021 including external packages) still lands at 0.0135, so the REFUSED verdict is not an artefact of counting npm imports as missing references.
